passages.original: , Petimus, carissimi, caritatem vestram ut quæ pro Mute vestra dicuntur attentius audiatis. In longum quidem Scripturae ordo digeritur ; sed vehit aliquantulum in memoriam teneatis, pauca vobis de pluribus coMmendamus. Dominus dicit in Evangelio : omnem decimationem vestram distribuite. Ipse per prophetam loquitur : .Inferte omnem decimam in horreum meum, ut sit cibus in domo mea; et probate me in his, dicit Dominns (Malach. III). Et in Exodo (Cap. XXIII) ; 1 Primitias terræ tuæ defer in domum Domini Dei tui. Paulus apostolus dicit: Filii Levi sacerdotium accipientes, mandatum habent decimas sumere a populo secundum legem (Hebr. VII), id est a fratribus suis; hilarem enim datorem diligit Deus (II Cor. IX). Salomon dixit : I Alii dividunt spolia, et ditiora fiunt; alii ragiunt non sua, et semper tn.egestate sunt (Prov. XI). Jesus filius Sirach dixit : In omni dato hitarem fac vultum tuum, et in exsultatione sanctifica decimas tuas, Da Altissimo secundum datum ejus; et in bono oculo adinventionem facito manuum tuarum, quoniam Dominus retribuens eat, et septies tantum reddet tibi (Eccli. XXXV). Augustinus dixit : decimas hæ etenim tributa sunt egentium animarum. Quod si decimam dederis, non solum abundantiam fructuum recipies, sed etiam sanitatem corporis consequeris. Decimae quidem ex debito requiruntur : quid si diceret Dens : Nempe meus es, o homo;
passages.english: We ask you, dearly beloved, in your charity, to listen more attentively to what is said for your salvation. The sequence of Scripture runs on at length; but so that you may keep at least a little in memory, we commend to you a few things out of many. The Lord says in the Gospel: "Distribute all your tithe." He himself speaks through the prophet: "Bring all the tithe into my storehouse, so that there may be food in my house; and test me in these things, says the Lord" (Malachi 3). And in Exodus (chapter 23): "Bring the first fruits of your land into the house of the Lord your God." The apostle Paul says: "The sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have a command to take tithes from the people according to the law" (Hebrews 7), that is, from their brothers; "for God loves a cheerful giver" (2 Corinthians 9). Solomon said: "Some divide spoils and become richer; others seize what is not theirs and are always in want" (Proverbs 11). Jesus son of Sirach said: "In every gift make your face cheerful, and sanctify your tithes with rejoicing. Give to the Most High according to what he has given, and with a good eye make the produce of your hands [an offering], for the Lord is one who repays, and he will give back to you seven times as much" (Ecclesiasticus 35). Augustine said: "For tithes are the tributes of needy souls. And if you give the tithe, you will not only receive an abundance of fruits, but you will also obtain health of body." Tithes indeed are required as a debt: what if God were to say: "Surely you are mine, O man;
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'Mute' read as 'salute'; 'vehit' as 'vel ut'; 'ragiunt' as 'rapiunt'; 'tn.egestate' as 'in egestate'; 'hitarem' as 'hilarem'; 'eat' as 'est'; 'Dens' as 'Deus'; 'Dominns' as 'Dominus'. Stray '1'/'I' before quotations treated as footnote marks. The first Gospel citation ('distribute all your tithe') does not match any Gospel verse closely; translated as given. 'decimas hæ' is ungrammatical; read as 'decimae'. The Augustine quotation is the sermon's attribution and may not be genuinely Augustine's.

passages.original: Quibus profecto verbis non præsentem solummodo 96 Judæorum quaestionem quam an ipse esset Christus interrogabant, explicavit; sed etiam hæreti. corum perfidia, quam futuram prævidit, quantum sit exsecranda, monstravit. Solus Arius enim dicit : Christus homo est tantum, Deus non est; at cum ipse dicat : Ego et Pater nnum sumus, manifeste patet quia unum cum Deo Patre substantialiter homo purus esse non potest. Et quia Christus idem quod Pater est, cavenda est hæresis Photini, quæ hoc credi prohibet.
passages.english: By these words he certainly did not only resolve the present question of the Jews, who were asking whether he himself was the Christ; but he also showed how much the faithlessness of the heretics, which he foresaw would come, is to be abhorred. For Arius alone says: "Christ is only a man, he is not God"; but since he himself says, "I and the Father are one," it is plainly evident that a mere man cannot be one in substance with God the Father. And because Christ is the same as the Father, the heresy of Photinus, which forbids this to be believed, must be guarded against.
passages.notes: "96" is a stray page or column number and has been omitted; "hæreti. corum" read as "hæreticorum" and "nnum" as "unum". "Solus Arius" ("Arius alone") is odd, since the view stated (Christ a mere man) is more usually attributed to Photinus, and the following context attributes a different view to Arius; the text may be corrupt here (perhaps for "Photinus" or a different word).

passages.original: Si enim in omni regno et natione filii regis libri sunt et immunes a vectigalibus, multo magis ille unus æterni Regis sub quo constituta sunt universa regna terrarum. Sequitur autem : Ut non scandalizemus eos, vade ad mare, et mitte hamum, et eum piscem qui primus ascenderit tolle. Et aperto ore ejus invenies staterem, et illum sumens, da eis pro me et pro te (Ibid.). Dicit beatus Hieronymus : Quid primum mirer in hoc loco; nescio præscientiam Domini aut magnitudinem. Præscientia namque illius admiranda est, quia agnovit quid in profundo maris ageretur, et quid piscis in ore gestaret, et quis de tanta multitudine primus ad hamum asceuderet.
passages.english: For if in every kingdom and nation the sons of the king are free and exempt from taxes, how much more that one [Son] of the eternal King, under whom all the kingdoms of the earth are established. And there follows: "So that we may not give offence to them, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the fish that comes up first. And when you open its mouth you will find a stater; take it and give it to them for me and for you" (ibid.). Blessed Jerome says: "What should I marvel at first in this passage, I do not know: the foreknowledge of the Lord or [his] greatness. For his foreknowledge is to be marvelled at, because he knew what was happening in the depth of the sea, and what the fish was carrying in its mouth, and which of so great a multitude would come up first to the hook."
